title.narrative: Increased capacity of constituents to develop labour market services and support transitions to decent work, particularly for youth and women

description.narrative:
The Egyptian labour market suffers from structural deficiencies that were exacerbated by the pandemic and recent geo-political tensions. Despite periods of economic growth, unemployment and inactivity, particularly among youth, remains stubbornly high. Egypt has also one of the lowest female labor participation rates globally and almost two thirds of all workers work in the informal economy, characterized by low decent work standards and limited social protection. To address these challenges, the ILO is working at both policy and operational level to test and institutionalize innovative approaches and to support an inclusive, ‘job rich growth’.
At the policy level, ILO will be supporting the Ministry of Labour to develop a comprehensive National Employment Strategy that aims to support job promotion both on the quantitative and the qualitative aspects with the involvement of all Ministries concerned. Dedicated capacity building will be provided to the Ministry of Labor to improve the quality and coverage of its employment services. Broad based tripartite and interministerial consultations conducted with the support of the ILO will support the drafting a national strategy for the transition of the informal to formal economy. A Green Job Assessment Model and analysis on export value chains will also be conducted to inform governmental partners on the impact of key public policies on employment.
Specific approaches will be tested to support access to decent work opportunities for the most vulnerable groups. The ILO EYE Forsa will expand employability and entrepreneurship support to women beneficiaires of the Takaful and Karama social protection programme in Asyut and Sharkiya governorates while PROSPECTS project will expand the access of forced displaced populations (FDP) and host communities (HC) to quality education and economic opportunities in particular in the care and IT sectors.
